name: Zand Bank
founded: 2021 (announced 12 Apr 2021; shareholders acquired a majority of Dubai Bank PJSC, Dec 2021; CBUAE banking licence received 30 Jun 2022, announced 5 Jul 2022)
regulators: SCA (UAE Capital Market Authority from 2026) — wealth management
ownership_summary: Unlisted PJSC. Shareholding percentages are not published. Zand's Aug 2026 release says it is backed by 'an Abu Dhabi ruling family-owned investment arm', Franklin Templeton, Aditya Birla Group (via Solfrid Investments), Mohamed Alabbar and Yusuff Ali; the 2022 board release names Al Hail Holding LLC and Global Development Group as represented shareholders. Existing shareholders injected a further AED 250m in Sep 2025, and the merger with related entity Eradah Capital LLC (completed 26 Dec 2025) raised paid-up capital to AED 2.35bn.

government_link: Indirect / unclear: Zand describes one backer as 'an Abu Dhabi ruling family-owned investment arm' (Aug 2026) but does not name it or its stake. No federal or emirate government shareholder disclosed. Checked 2026-10-12.
group_structure: Zand Bank PJSC with one wholly owned subsidiary, Zand Trust LLC S.O.C. (incorporated 12 May 2025), which issues the AED-backed stablecoin. The Dec 2024 general assembly also approved a Zand Group governance structure including a holding company; whether it has been set up was not found. Paid-up capital AED 2.35bn after the 26 Dec 2025 merger with related entity Eradah Capital LLC. ZandTrust has its own site (zandtrust.com).
footprint: UAE (Dubai-headquartered, digital-only; no branch network found). Technology capabilities set up in Asia (2024 CEO letter). Checked 2026-10-12.
customer_segments: Government and GREs, mid-to-large corporates, SMEs, fintechs, virtual asset service providers, real estate developers (escrow), and professional investors / HNW individuals through Zand Wealth.
business_lines: Corporate and transaction banking; treasury and global markets; real estate and commercial escrow; Banking-as-a-Service and payments (Zand Pay, blockchain payment gateway); digital asset custody (VARA-licensed, Dec 2024) and tokenisation (ZandMint); AED-backed stablecoin via Zand Trust (Nov 2025); AI-as-a-service; Zand Wealth (wealth management and personal banking for professional investors: funds, equities, bonds, structured products, alternatives, digital-asset investments, bespoke portfolio management).

capabilities.wealth_summary: Zand is a corporate- and digital-asset-focused digital bank that has added a wealth arm, ZandWealth, described as 'wealth management and personal banking designed for professional investors'. The page lists investment funds, equities, bonds, structured products, alternatives (which 'may include private market strategies, multi-strategy hedge funds'), digital-asset investments and bespoke portfolio management, plus in-app portfolio view and VARA-licensed digital-asset custody. Its enquiry form bands clients by net assets (below AED 2m, AED 2–4m, AED 4–10m, above AED 10m). The 2024 CEO letter set 'launching our wealth and asset management services' as a 2025 goal, and the 2025 org chart includes a Head of Wealth & AM. No launch date, product providers, custodians or client numbers for ZandWealth are published.

asset_management.detail: The 2025 org chart has a 'Head of Wealth & AM' and the 2024 CEO letter targeted launching wealth and asset management services; no Zand-managed funds or AUM found.

brokerage.detail: ZandWealth lists access to listed equities ('regional and global growth themes') and bonds; execution venue, broker and markets not named. Wealth management is licensed by SCA / Capital Market Authority.

digital_investing.detail: The Zand app lets clients 'view and manage your investments' and monitor portfolios in real time, and hold digital assets in custody; self-directed in-app trading is not described.

advisory.detail: 'Tailored investment strategies and portfolio solutions designed around your financial goals, risk appetite, and investment preferences'.

discretionary.detail: 'Bespoke portfolio management' listed under ZandWealth; mandate type not specified.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No model or robo portfolios on the ZandWealth page.

funds_platform.detail: 'A broad selection of professionally managed funds across asset classes, sectors, and regions'; fund platform or managers not named (Franklin Templeton is a shareholder but is not named as a fund provider).

structured_products.detail: Listed on ZandWealth: 'tailored investment solutions designed to meet specific market views'; issuers not named.

private_markets.detail: 'Alternative Investments' category that 'may include private market strategies, multi-strategy hedge funds and other non-traditional asset classes'; no product or manager named. Separately, Zand provides custody/banking for Tokinvest's tokenised real-world assets (Apr 2025).

opportunities: ZandWealth lists funds, structured products, alternatives/private markets, bonds, equities and digital assets for professional investors, but names no product providers, platforms or managers (S3).
Wealth and asset management is a stated build-out: 2025 goal in the 2024 CEO letter; Head of Wealth & AM in the 2025 org chart (S5, S4).
Positions itself as a bridge between traditional and digital finance, with VARA custody and tokenisation already live (S3, S14, S15).
barriers: Small balance sheet and young franchise: deposits just over AED 5bn and net profit AED 34m in 2025 (S4).
Main franchise is corporate, GRE and digital-asset banking; no retail investing app or client numbers published (S2, S4).
Franklin Templeton is a shareholder with a board seat, which may shape fund-shelf choices (S8).
No financial statements or Pillar 3 disclosures published online, which limits due diligence (S22).
